test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is the relative measure of dispersion?
solution:
The correct answer is** Coefficient of variation.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coefficient of variation:**

 
 
• The coefficient of variation (CV) is a relative measure of dispersion that indicates the extent of variability in relation to the mean of the population.
 
• It is calculated as the ratio of the standard deviation to the mean, often expressed as a percentage.
 
• In a financial enterprise, CV is useful for comparing the degree of variation from one data series to another, even if the means are drastically different. This is particularly useful in risk assessment and portfolio management.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Variance:**

 
 
• Variance is an absolute measure of dispersion that calculates the average of the squared differences from the mean.
 
• While it gives insights into the data's spread, it does not provide a relative perspective. Hence, it is not suitable for comparing datasets with different units or scales.
 
 
 
• **Range:**
 
 
• Range is the difference between the maximum and minimum values in a dataset. It is a simple measure of dispersion but does not consider the distribution of all data points.
 
• It is an absolute measure and does not account for the mean or standard deviation, making it less useful for relative comparisons.
 
 
 
• **Mean deviation:**
 
 
• Mean deviation, or average absolute deviation, measures the average of the absolute differences between each data point and the mean.
 
• Like variance, it is an absolute measure and does not provide a relative sense of variability, making it less useful for comparing datasets with different scales.
